key_insight: A conditional flow-matching generative model can rapidly synthesize realistic 3D instantaneous urban wind and temperature fields by conditioning on building geometry and mean flow.
engineering_relevance: This enables turbulence-aware urban microclimate design and climate adaptation studies with LES-like detail in seconds instead of expensive iterative simulation.
method: Uses Conditional Flow Matching to generate stochastic 3D velocity and temperature fields.
Conditions generation on urban geometry and mean-flow information to guide physically plausible outputs.
Runs in overlapping pixel-space blocks with shared-noise initialization to reduce GPU memory use while preserving spatial continuity.
evidence_signal: Compared with LES reference data, the surrogate achieved low NRMSE for first-order statistics (2.99% wind, 1.77% temperature) and strong agreement for turbulence metrics, TKE, PDFs, and vertical profiles.
watch_item: Because it generates fields in overlapping pixel-space chunks, careful handling is needed to avoid seam artifacts and to ensure generalization across unseen urban morphologies.
paper_title: Conditional Flow Matching for Generation of 3D Multi-variable Instantaneous Urban Microclimate Fields
